report: Tom was given a shower this morning, and his dental prostheses were cleaned thoroughly. He required assistance with dressing and brushing his teeth. Tom enjoyed a brief walk in the garden, assisted by a nurse. He complained of back pain and was given pain medication as per his care plan. His family visited in the afternoon and discussed updating his pyjamas and slippers.

Linda needed full assistance with washing and getting dressed today. Her moisturiser was applied to her skin to prevent dryness. She ate her breakfast with encouragement, needing adapted cutlery. Linda participated in the group singing activity for a short while but appeared restless and confused at times. Her toenails have grown too long and will need to be trimmed soon.

George was assisted with a sponge bath and had his eyes cleaned with prescribed eyedrops. He remained in bed most of the day due to fatigue and shortness of breath. George did not finish his lunch but kept well-hydrated with frequent sips of water. He had a family call to update him on medication reorders. This afternoon, George seemed more agitated and needed reassurance frequently.

Emily required help with washing her face and brushing her teeth. Her dietary intake was poor, and she needed full assistance to eat her breakfast. She spent the morning in the living room flipping through magazines but seemed withdrawn. Emily’s legs showed signs of oedema, and this was documented for the doctor’s review. Her family was informed about the need for a new pair of slippers.

Michael received a bed bath and was assisted with applying moisturiser to his legs. He used his wheelchair to go to the social room but sat quietly for most of the morning, showing signs of apathy. Michael reported mild chest tightness, which subsided after a rest. His family visited and had a care plan discussion with the nurse regarding his pain management. His physical condition will be monitored closely over the next few days.

John was assisted with shaving and dressing this morning. After breakfast, he expressed severe back pain which was managed with medication. He spent some quiet time in the garden. Later in the evening, John needed full assistance to get ready for bed. Hydration and nutrition were closely monitored, with encouragement given for fluid intake. His family was updated about his condition.

Marian experienced significant shortness of breath today and was administered her prescribed inhaler. She was given support with brushing her teeth and cleaning her dentures. During the afternoon, Marian played cards with other residents but was visibly tired. Assistance was required during lunch as she struggled with her adapted cutlery. Her ongoing confusion was noted and appropriate measures were taken.

Beth's pain levels were high this morning, so her palliative care team adjusted her pain relief medication. Assistance was provided for showering and applying cream to her peeled and red skin. During the social room activity, Beth needed continuous encouragement to eat and drink. Her nails were trimmed as they were too long. By evening, she participated in a calm reading session before going to bed with help.

Michael wandered restlessly throughout the night; caregivers ensured his safety and readjusted him in bed as needed. Morning care included shaving and changing his pyjamas, which were newly supplied by his family. He joined the painting session but showed signs of agitation and confusion. During lunch, special attention was given to avoid choking incidents. His care plan was reviewed with a focus on his increasing restlessness and pain management.

Gertrude had a restless night, experiencing nausea but stabilising after medication. Friday started with assistance in showering, and thorough care was provided for her dental prostheses. She involved herself minimally in the social room's group activity, preferring to flip through a magazine. Redness and itching of her skin were noted and treated with topical cream. Her hydration levels were monitored, and she was encouraged to drink more fluids through the day.

Robert was given a sponge bath this morning, and assistance with brushing his teeth. His oral medications were administered. In the late afternoon, he enjoyed browsing through a magazine in the lounge. Robert's family was informed about his need for more comfortable slippers. He exhibited slight confusion when asked about his dinner preference.

Theresa had her morning wash and eye drops administered. Her legs were moisturized, and she was assisted in choosing an outfit for the day. Theresa ate most of her breakfast but required some encouragement. Later, she interacted with a few other residents during a quiet armchair exercise session. She reported mild nausea in the evening.

Michael received help with showering and dressing. His dental prosthesis was cleaned, and he completed his hydration and nutrition log. Michael enjoyed a brief walk in the garden with a care aide supervising him closely. He expressed discomfort due to mild back pain and was repositioned in bed several times throughout the day.

Grace was assisted with her full morning routine, including brushing her teeth and applying cream to her legs. She participated in the arts and crafts activity, painting quietly with the group. Her daughter visited in the afternoon, and they spent time chatting in the social room. Grace mentioned experiencing sporadic shortness of breath, which was closely monitored.

Peter was given a thorough wash and was assisted in getting dressed for the day. He needed help eating his breakfast, and his water intake was recorded. In the afternoon, his nails were trimmed, and a moisturizing lotion was applied due to mild skin redness. Peter attended the music activity but appeared somewhat apathetic and disengaged. His care plan was reviewed with his family, and they agreed to order more pain relief medication for his chronic discomfort.

Resident John was assisted in washing before receiving his morning medications. Though weak, he seemed to enjoy a brief chat with fellow residents in the lounge after. He needed full assistance during lunch and was encouraged to drink more water. He experienced mild nausea which was managed with prescribed medication. Stools were regular. His daughter visited him in the afternoon and discussed upcoming changes to his care plan with the nursing team.

Martha participated in a painting activity this morning after being helped with brushing her teeth and dressing. She needed help transferring from her wheelchair and was monitored closely due to previous falls. Martha consumed half of her breakfast and required some encouragement to finish her soup at lunch. Mild confusion noted during the afternoon. She complained of minor back pain which was alleviated with repositioning.

Resident Alan was given a shower and new dressing for his pressure ulcers first thing in the morning. Hydration and nutrition were monitored, as he only ate sporadically. During the afternoon, he joined others for a movie but showed signs of agitation and restlessness. Assistance was required for him to use the bathroom, and his nails, previously noted as being too long, were trimmed. His wife communicated that she wishes to discuss palliative care strategies.

Betty required help with oral care and was dressed and ready for the day by mid-morning. She was unable to attend the exercise session as usual and stayed in her room where she read with some difficulty. Betty declined lunch but took some sips of juice through an adapted cup. There was noted redness on her legs which was treated with a topical application. In the later part of the day, she appeared more confused and restless and was given mild sedatives as per her care plan.

Mike woke up disoriented and restless, requiring help throughout the night to adjust his position in bed to alleviate discomfort. He participated in the group’s reading session in the late morning but needed regular reminders to stay hydrated. His urinary output was normal but stools were looser than usual. Assisted with dental care and dressed comfortably in the afternoon. Informed family of the loose stools and upcoming medication review.

John was given his morning medications along with his COPD nebulizer session. Staff observed significant swelling in his ankles and administered prescribed diuretics. He participated in the singing activity, which seemed to elevate his mood. At night, he experienced some confusion and needed assistance to settle in bed. The family was informed about ordering more pain medication.

Lisa required full assistance with dressing and bathing this morning. She managed to eat half of her breakfast with encouragement and a specially adapted spoon. During the afternoon, she enjoyed browsing through a magazine but appeared fatigued and napped shortly afterward. There was a mild episode of nausea in the evening, promptly addressed with antiemetic medication. Lisa's son has inquired about a new wheelchair cushion to alleviate pressure sores.

Margaret was provided with her morning wash and oral hygiene, including her dental prostheses. She had a restless night with frequent trips to the toilet, necessitating additional care. Ate all of her lunch but needed encouragement to keep hydrated throughout the day. Her pressure ulcer dressing was changed, and some redness was noted. Staff documented interactions with her daughter, who requested detailed daily updates.

Michael enjoyed a morning walk in the garden with assistance and engaged in the memory game activity in the social room. His evening was marked by heightened agitation, requiring a calming environment and some PRN medication. The palliative care nurse discussed his ongoing discomfort due to back pain; adjustments to his pain management plan are underway. He complained of breathlessness before bed but settled down with the use of his oxygen therapy.

Eleanor needed full support with her morning routine, including bathing and dressing. Her breakfast and dinner consumption were noted to be minimal, prompting staff to offer high-calorie shakes for additional nutrition. She fell asleep reading a book in the afternoon, showing signs of extreme fatigue. Discussions about her end-of-life care preferences took place, with family members via a video call, ensuring their wishes align with her comfort needs.
